He played college basketball for the [[University of Kansas]][http://www.kuathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/taylor_tyshawn00.html KUathletics.com Profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120705154226/http://www.kuathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/taylor_tyshawn00.html |date=July 5, 2012 }} before he was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the 41st overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Taylor attended [[St. Anthony High School (New Jersey)|St. Anthony High School]] in New Jersey where he played under renowned high school coach [[Bob Hurley]]. During the 2007–08 season, Taylor's team went 32–0 and was awarded the high school basketball [[mythical national championship]] by [[USA Today]]. Taylor also appeared in the 2009 film ''The Street Stops Here'', a documentary about Hurley and St. Anthony.[https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1162126/ The Street Stops Here – IMDB] Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Taylor was listed as the No. 11 point guard and the No. 77 player in the nation in 2008.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Tyshawn-Taylor-60259;_ylt=Audi1xRra9A2uxkDyhs7..BGPZB4 Tyshawn Taylor Recruiting Profile] ==College career== In 2008–09, Taylor averaged 9.7 points and 3.0 assists per game as he earned Big 12 All-Rookie team honors. Taylor changed his KU jersey number from 15 to 10 prior to his sophomore year and averaged 7.2 points and 3.4 assists per game on the [[2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team]] who won both the Big 12 regular season and tournament championships. Taylor averaged 9.3 points and 4.6 assists his junior year. Taylor led the team in assists and was fourth in the Big 12. On February 21, 2011, Taylor was suspended indefinitely from the team for violating team rules. The specifics of the suspension were not announced.{{Cite web |date=2011-02-21 |title=No. 2 Kansas suspends guard Taylor indefinitely |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=6144510 |access-date=2024-10-11 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}} Starting for the fourth straight year, Taylor nearly doubled his career scoring average. Taylor, along with All-American [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]], helped lead Kansas to the 2012 national championship game before losing to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]. ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- |style="text-align:left;"|[[2008–09 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2008–09]] |style="text-align:left;"|[[2008–09 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] |35||33||26.5||'''.506'''||.364||'''.724'''||2.2||3.0||1.1||.2||9.7 |- |- |style="text-align:left;"|[[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]] |style="text-align:left;"|[[2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] |36||25||23.1||.438||.339||.716||'''2.4'''||3.4||1.3||.2||7.2 |- |style="text-align:left;"|[[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11]] |style="text-align:left;"|[[2010–11 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] |36||31||27.1||.479||.380||.719||1.9||4.6||1.0||'''.3'''|||9.3 |- |style="text-align:left;"|[[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011–12]] |style="text-align:left;"|[[2011–12 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] |'''39'''||'''38'''||'''33.4'''||.477||'''.382'''||.688||2.3||'''4.8'''||'''1.3'''||.2||'''16.6''' |- | style="text-align:left;"| Career | style="text-align:left;"| |146||127||27.7||.477||.370||.708||2.2||3.9||1.2||.2||10.8 {{S-end}} ==Professional career== === Brooklyn Nets (2012–2014) === On June 28, 2012, Taylor was selected with the 41st overall pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He was later traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for cash considerations. On July 6, 2012, he signed with the Nets.{{cite web|title=Nets sign 2nd round pick Taylor|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/06/taylor-nets.ap/|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2012|access-date=July 6, 2012}} When [[Deron Williams]] was ruled out for final two games before the All-Star break with [[ankle problems]], Taylor was put into the Nets' rotation.{{cite web|last=Lorenzo|first=Tom|title=Deron Williams to miss next two games, will return after the All-Star break|url=http://www.netsdaily.com/2013/2/11/3977256/deron-williams-to-miss-next-two-games-will-return-after-the-all-star|work=NetsDaily.com|date=February 11, 2013|access-date=February 11, 2013}} In his first game in the rotation, Taylor finished with a career-high 12 points in a career-high 34 minutes as the Nets defeated the [[Indiana Pacers]] 89–84 in overtime.{{cite web|title=Rapid Reaction: Nets 89, Pacers 84 (OT)|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/brooklyn-nets/post/_/id/8645/rapid-reaction-nets-89-pacers-84-ot|work=ESPN.com|date=February 11, 2013|access-date=February 11, 2013}} On November 25, in a loss against the Los Angeles Lakers, coach [[Jason Kidd]] asked Taylor to "accidentally" bump into him because the Nets were out of timeouts. This incident was highlighted as evidence that Coach Kidd was out of his league as a rookie coach.[http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24292950/video-jason-kidd-tells-tyshawn-taylor-to-hit-him-to-force-timeout VIDEO: Jason Kidd tells Tyshawn Taylor to hit him to force timeout] During his rookie and sophomore seasons, he had multiple assignments with the [[Springfield Armor]] of the [[NBA D-League]].[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html 2012–13 NBA Assignments] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327190108/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |date=March 27, 2014 }}[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html 23, 2020}} ===Retirement=== On October 25, 2021, Taylor announced his retirement.{{cite tweet |author=Tyshawn Taylor|user=tyshawntaylor|number = 1452832763753730049 |date=October 25, 2021|title=Retirement}} ==The Basketball Tournament (TBT)== In the summer of 2017, Taylor, for the third year, competed in [[The Basketball Tournament]] on [[ESPN]] for Team FOE, a [[Philadelphia]] based team coached by [[NBA]] forwards [[Markieff Morris|Markieff]] and [[Marcus Morris (basketball)|Marcus Morris]]. In four games, Taylor averaged 12.8 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game as Team FOE advanced to the Super 16 Round in [[Brooklyn, New York]]. FOE lost 72–67 in the Super 16 against Boeheim's Army, a team composed of [[Syracuse University]] basketball alum. Taylor also competed in TBT in 2015 and 2016 as well. In 2016, his first season with Team FOE, Taylor averaged 17.0 points and 3.7 rebounds over the course of three games.
